subject: Time Series of Distance Sampling Data

messages.author: 7dfbeaa79098bc2c
messages.subject: Time Series of Distance Sampling Data
parts:
Dear All,

I need some help in finding distance sampling data sets with temporal dimension (preferably yearly time series). I am aware of one dataset analysed by Moore and Barlow (2011) for estimating trend in fin whale abundance. However, the dataset is not available to download from the paper appendices. I'll be grateful if you can guide me to any resources from where I can obtain such a dataset.

Reference:

Moore, J.E. & Barlow, J. (2011) Bayesian state-space model of fin whale abundance trends from a 1991-2008 time series of line-transect surveys in the California Current. Journal of Applied Ecology, 48, 1195–1205.


Thanks,
Khurram

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: Time Series of Distance Sampling Data
parts:
Hi Khurram,

I'm an author on the following papers, all of which analyze distance sampling time series data (although not all annual).  I do not own any of these datasets, but if you contact the primary authors explaining why you want it, I expect they'd be happy to send the data along.  You could try the same approach with the authors of the paper you cite.

Best wishes,

 - Len Thomas

These papers are available for download from my web site (www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/len/pubs.html)

Campbell, G.S., K. Whitaker, L. Thomas, A. Douglas, J. Calambokidis and J.A. Hildebrand. In press.  Inter-annual and seasonal trends in cetacean distribution, density and abundance in waters off southern California. Deep Sea Research II.

Durant, S., M. Craft, R. Hilborn, S. Bashir, J. Hando and L. Thomas. 2011. Long term trends in carnivore abundance using distance sampling in Serengeti national park, Tanzania. Journal of Applied Ecology 48: 1490-1500.

Thomas, L., K.P. Burnham & S.T Buckland. 2004. Temporal inferences from distance sampling surveys. Chapter 5 in Buckland, S.T., D.R. Anderson, K.P. Burnham, J.L. Laake, D.L. Borchers & L. Thomas (Eds.), Advanced Distance Sampling. Oxford University Press. (Buckland would be the person to contact about these data, in the first instance.)
